name: comparator-regeneration
description: Decision time versus input overdrive over PVT at 50 mV / 1 mV / 0.1 mV, the regeneration time constant tau extracted from the two small rungs, the near-metastable behaviour at 0.1 mV, and the switching energy and static current per decision.
claim: sim/dut.json binds design/comparator.spice (id comparator-dr0001, provenance schematic), the ratified topology from spec/decision-records/0001-comparator-topology.md ('DR-0001'). This record substantiates that a three-overdrive transient regeneration sweep genuinely runs and tau is genuinely extracted from it, on that design, over the full PVT grid. Unlike the offset-MC and preamp-noise benches, this bench is transient and unaffected by DR-0001 Decision Section 3's DC-resolvable-front-end finding -- but it is STILL NOT evidence toward README.md#target-specification's Decision-time-vs-overdrive row: that ratification is a separate, later act (spec/porting-plan.md's third step in this chain).
analyses: meas tran vsup_v find v(vdd) at=25n
meas tran td_a trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(dan) val=0.5 rise=1 td=35n
meas tran td_b trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(dbn) val=0.5 rise=1 td=35n
meas tran td_c trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(dcn) val=0.5 rise=1 td=35n
meas tran da_first find v(dan) at=18n
meas tran db_first find v(dbn) at=18n
meas tran dc_first find v(dcn) at=18n
meas tran da_end find v(dan) at=55n
meas tran db_end find v(dbn) at=55n
meas tran dc_end find v(dcn) at=55n
meas tran i_stat avg i(vsupa) from=25n to=29n
meas tran q_dec integ i(vsupa) from=39.9n to=48n

td_od50_ns.description: PRIMARY CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR as well as the row-facing number. The min/max pair is a sanity envelope, not the spec bound: 1 ps would mean the delay measurement latched onto a numerical artefact, and 25 ns is most of the strobe window. The SPEC bound (README.md's decision-time row) is deliberately NOT encoded while README.md's target-specification table stays DRAFT/unratified (ratification is spec/porting-plan.md's separate third step). The per-axis floors are what make --sabotage-corners fail: regeneration speed is set by device transconductance, which is corner- and temperature-sensitive. Floors calibrated from this experiment's first committed 45-point record (named in this experiment's README.md, run --no-write during issue #8 development, taken against the then-bound placeholder DUT), with ~40% margin below the observed weakest slices (process 2.61%, temperature 12.76%). The supply axis is unfloored because the delay threshold is supply-normalized on purpose (see the deck header), which removes most of the supply dependence from the measurement by construction (observed weakest supply slice: 2.02%). NOTE: sim/dut.json now binds design/comparator.spice (provenance schematic); the temperature-axis floor here is a known FAIL against that real DUT's own transistor-level regeneration speed (observed weakest slice 2.73% against the 8.0% floor above) -- this is a real measured property, not a plumbing bug, and this issue deliberately does not recalibrate it (see design/README.md's 'Open items' for the tracked follow-up).

tau_ps.description: Regeneration time constant, extracted from the (1 mV, 0.1 mV) pair -- both inside the logarithmic region, one decade apart, so tau = (t(0.1 mV) - t(1 mV))/ln(10). Bounds are a sanity envelope: a negative or sub-0.1 ps tau means the two delays came out in the wrong order, and 20 ns means the structure is not regenerating on the timescale of the strobe.

resolve_decades.description: How many e-folds of regeneration fit inside the measured 1 mV decision time (td_od1 / tau). It is the metastability lever arm: the probability of an unresolved decision falls as exp(-t/tau), so this is the exponent that number is taken to.

dout_od50_end.description: POLARITY CHECK: after the second strobe the 50 mV instance must hold the POSITIVE answer (dout normalized to its own supply). Together with dout_od50_first below it proves the same instance decided BOTH ways within one run.

dout_od01_end.description: the same at 0.1 mV overdrive -- i.e. the near-metastable rung still resolves to the CORRECT answer within the strobe window, which is the statement the metastability row rests on.

dout_od50_first.description: the OPPOSITE-polarity half of the same proof: at the first strobe the input was negative, so the held output must be low.

i_static_ua.description: Static supply current of one instance with the strobe low. A floor only: zero would mean the bias never came up and every dynamic number in this record was taken on a dead circuit.

e_dec_fj.description: SWITCHING ENERGY PER DECISION, added as a real check now that sim/dut.json binds a transistor-level decision stage (design/comparator.spice) -- see this note's own prior trigger condition in evidence.notes below. abs(q_dec - i_stat*8.1e-9)*vsup_v integrates the supply current over the second-strobe decision window, nets out the static-bias baseline, and converts to energy; the abs() means this is a magnitude sanity envelope, not a spec bound (README.md has no energy-per-decision row). Bounds are deliberately loose (roughly 30x either side of the first transistor-level 45-point record's observed ~31-61 fJ span, named in this experiment's README.md) to catch a wrong-sign/wrong-units/collapsed-to-residue regression, not to pin the design's actual switching energy.

notes: MISMATCH-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION (the plain mos corner set). Regeneration time and offset are separable effects and are budgeted separately.
THE DELAY IS MEASURED ON THE SECOND STROBE, where the output must actively flip a latch holding the opposite answer.
TIMING THRESHOLDS ARE SUPPLY-NORMALIZED (each output divided by its own supply, crossed at 0.5).
METASTABILITY IS A FIRST-CLASS ROW HERE, not a note. tau and resolve_decades are recorded at every PVT point.

e_dec_fj NOW CARRIES A CHECK (issue #20). The prior placeholder DUT's decision stage was behavioural and drew no supply current at all, so the switching energy measured against it was the FRONT END's alone and what remained of the charge integral was dominated by numerical residue -- this note originally said a check belonged here the moment a transistor-level decision stage was bound in sim/dut.json. sim/dut.json now binds design/comparator.spice, whose decision stage is transistor-level and draws real dynamic (and static) supply current, so e_dec_fj is a genuine front-end-plus-decision-stage switching energy; see checks.e_dec_fj.description above for the bound.

THE TARG SEARCHES START AT td=35n, PORTED FROM gf180-comparator's fix (its own PR history): a real comparator's output SR latch has no defined power-up state, so an unwindowed targ search can lock onto the t=0 metastable-resolution transient instead of the strobe-driven decision under test. 35 ns is after the first strobe has completed and after the 20 ns input flip has settled, and before the second strobe at 40 ns.

SOLVER TOLERANCES. reltol = 1e-4 and vntol = 1e-9 are tightened from the ngspice defaults so that a sub-nanosecond delay difference between two overdrives is resolved rather than smeared. abstol is 1e-13, matching gf180-comparator's finding that 1e-15 (the kickback deck's tighter setting) makes some points of this grid fail to take their first transient step at all.
